block.comment: Use Timer1 to count at 10 Hz while loop remains available. Upload, connect Plotter at 115200 baud, then Start. The board sends the complete layout and instructions.
The interrupt changes this counter. Keep the handler short and copy the value atomically before displaying it.
100000 microseconds = 0.1 second. Change this period to change the interrupt rate. Timer1 is reserved; do not combine this lesson with a Timer1 motor or Servo engine.
Fixed incoming line buffer, including room for a terminator. Charts, images and the JSON header stay on the computer/Flash, not in this array.

block.comment: Read one complete newline-terminated command. Partial lines stay in a fixed byte buffer. CR is ignored; oversized commands are discarded. There is no String allocation or waiting for bytes. Expand this reusable function to see the ordinary array and logic blocks.

block.comment: Send the same dashboard on boot and on Start. Edit this Serial text to change its appearance.
Announce the dashboard before loop. The Timer1 block starts its configured interrupt at the end of setup.
Copy or clear the shared counter atomically: an interrupt must not change half of a multibyte value during this operation.
Use elapsed milliseconds instead of delay. The command reader remains responsive between updates; unsigned subtraction also works when millis wraps.
Read complete commands, then copy and display the counter five times per second. The interrupt itself runs ten times per second; no delay blocks command handling.
